target.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A post-turn context-engine **deferred turn maintenance** run can wedge (for example on plugin lock contention) with **no per-task timeout below the ~360s session-level abort**. While it is wedged it holds its maintenance lane, so a user message queued behind it on the same session can wait minutes before being processed, even though the model is healthy. `session.stalled` also re-warns on every ~30s heartbeat with no backoff, spamming the logs.

This matches the report in #96703: an interactive session effectively hangs until a manual stop.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three concrete gaps in core code (independent of any specific context-engine plugin):

1. **No per-task timeout was available on the maintenance enqueue.** `scheduleDeferredTurnMaintenance` enqueued the maintenance worker via `enqueueCommandInLane(...)` with no options. The command queue already supports a per-task timeout (`taskTimeoutMs` → rejects with `CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError` and releases the lane), but the maintenance lane never wired it up, so an operator hitting the wedge had no knob below the session-level abort.
2. **A timed-out maintenance worker was not fenced.** Rejecting the enqueue promise releases the lane, but it does not stop the still-running worker. A wedged worker could later call `runtimeContext.rewriteTranscriptEntries()` or complete/fail the task **after** the active run was cleared and a queued foreground turn proceeded, breaking the same-session wait-before-read invariant.
3. **`session.stalled` had no log backoff.** `session.stuck` and `session.long_running` already throttle repeats; `session.stalled` did not.

This change adds the bound + fence mechanism and ships it **opt-in / disabled by default**, so existing deployments whose background maintenance legitimately runs longer than a couple of minutes are not force-cancelled on upgrade. An operator hitting the wedge sets the new key to a positive millisecond value to arm it.

## User Impact

- **No behavior change on upgrade unless configured.** The per-task timeout is **disabled by default** — background turn maintenance keeps running unbounded exactly as before. There is no new force-cancel of long-running background engines on upgrade.
- Operators experiencing the wedge **opt in** by setting `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs` to a positive millisecond value (absent or `0` keeps it disabled). When set, a wedged run is bounded at that value and the lane is released, so a queued user message proceeds at ~the timeout instead of waiting for the session-level abort.
- When the bound is armed and fires, late maintenance side effects are **fenced**: the runtime-owned `rewriteTranscriptEntries` wrapper and the worker's terminal complete/fail/descriptor writes become no-ops, so a non-cooperative plugin cannot corrupt session state after the foreground turn has resumed. When the bound is disabled, the fence is never armed.
- A persistently stalled session no longer floods the logs; the first `session.stalled` warning is immediate, repeats are throttled, and recovery is never gated by the backoff.

### Changes

- `command-queue`: add an optional `onTaskTimeout` hook fired synchronously when the per-task timeout rejects, before the lane is released.
- `context-engine-maintenance`: resolve an **opt-in** per-task timeout from `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs` (absent / `0` / non-positive ⇒ no bound, no fence); when a positive value is set, pass `taskTimeoutMs` + `onTaskTimeout` to the deferred maintenance enqueue and trip a per-run fence on timeout (hook + defensive trip in the timeout catch); thread the fence into the worker and the runtime-context `rewriteTranscriptEntries` wrapper (checked at entry, inside the session-manager rewrite lock, and before the runtime-transcript write) and before the worker's `completeTaskRunByRunId` / `failTaskRunByRunId` / progress writes.
- `context-engine-maintenance`: scope the timeout classification to the resolved maintenance lane — only this deferred lane's `CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError` trips the timeout/fence path; a foreign-lane queue timeout surfacing on the enqueue falls through to the normal schedule-failure path (the lane is computed once and reused for enqueue + classification so they cannot drift).
- `session.stalled`: apply the existing `session.stuck`/`session.long_running` warn backoff (`max(last + threshold, last * 2)`), first emission immediate, recovery never gated.
- Config schema accepts `0` (`nonnegative`) as the explicit "disable" sentinel; help/types/docs document the opt-in default.
- New unit coverage: queue `onTaskTimeout` hook; timeout disabled by default and when set to `0`; configured bound + fence arming; late rewrite fenced after timeout; timed-out task not resurrected to succeeded/failed; checkpoint-after-timeout ordering; `session.stalled` backoff.

## Evidence

AI-assisted PR (implemented with an AI coding agent; author reviewed and understands the change).

**Static / unit validation** (this branch):
- `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:test:src` — clean
- `command-queue.test.ts` — 34 passed; `context-engine-maintenance.test.ts` — 60 passed (incl. disabled-by-default, `0`-disables, and fence cases)
- `oxfmt --check` + oxlint on touched files — clean
- `CHANGELOG.md` not touched (left for maintainers at landing)

**Real runtime reproduction (end-to-end, in a container).** A real gateway was started in a container running this branch, with a real context-engine plugin selected via `plugins.slots.contextEngine` whose `info.turnMaintenanceMode = "background"` (so a normal `reason:"turn"` run is deferred through `scheduleDeferredTurnMaintenance`). Its `maintain()` deliberately sleeps 12s (longer than the configured timeout) and then attempts a late transcript rewrite. The bound was **explicitly opted in** for the test: `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs = 5000`. Two real agent turns were run on one session. Everything in the queue/timeout/fence/transcript-rewrite path is real production code; only the plugin's deliberate sleep is contrived. Logs redacted (provider/model/host/ids replaced with placeholders):

```
[T+0.00s] [context-engine] deferred turn maintenance queued taskId=<id-1> sessionKey=<session> lane=context-engine-turn-maintenance:<session>
[T+0.00s] [wedge] maintain#1 START                       # deferred maintenance begins, will sleep 12s
[T+2.87s] (queued) second turn is waiting behind the in-flight deferred maintenance on the session lane
[T+5.00s] [diagnostic] lane task error: lane=context-engine-turn-maintenance:<session> durationMs=5000 error="CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError: ... task timed out after 5000ms"
[T+5.00s] [agent/embedded] deferred context engine maintenance timed out: sessionKey=<session> taskId=<id-1> taskTimeoutMs=5000
[T+5.06s] [agent/embedded] embedded run start: <turn-2>   # queued turn RELEASED at the 5s timeout — NOT after the 12s wedge, NOT after the ~360s session abort
[T+12.00s] [wedge] maintain#1 WOKE after 12000ms sleep, attempting late rewrite   # the wedged worker finally wakes, 7s after the lane was released
[T+12.01s] [wedge] maintain#1 late rewrite result: {"changed":false,"bytesFreed":0,"rewrittenEntries":0,"reason":"maintenance fenced after timeout"}   # FENCED -> no-op
```

Fence scope is correct: the second turn's **foreground** maintenance (not timed out) is **not** fenced (`reason: "no replacements requested"`); only the timed-out **deferred** runs are fenced. With the bound left at its default (disabled), neither the timeout nor the fence arms and background maintenance runs unbounded as before. A scripted reproduction is available on request.

Closes #96703

## Summary
- detect progress-only Slack tool chrome payloads with leading tool emoji plus command/status body
- convert thread-scoped chrome to reactions instead of `chat.postMessage`
- fail closed by suppressing chrome without a reaction target while preserving semantic replies
- type automatic tool-progress payloads at the producer boundary with a closed generic plugin-SDK progress intent so Slack does not infer from arbitrary text

## What Problem This Solves
Progress-only operational chrome like `:hammer_and_wrench: \`pnpm test\`` or `:writing_hand: Write: MEMORY.md` can leak into Slack as user-visible messages when a tool/status payload accidentally reaches the Slack send path. This creates noise in working channels and violates the progress-chrome pre-send gate. The Slack extension now classifies only narrow progress-only payloads and prevents them from becoming chat posts.

target.title: feat(browser): add secure per-tab copilot panel
target.body:
Related: #93680

## What Problem This Solves

The browser side-panel copilot needs one isolated agent session per tab without letting page content, another tab, or a stale panel acquire a different browser target or receive another session's events. Closing a tab must also end live delivery and run custody without deleting its transcript.

## Why This Change Was Made

This rebuild gives the browser copilot a dedicated canonical device-pairing identity with issued-token reuse, Gateway-owned session subscription allowlists with pre-delivery filtering, and typed tab bindings enforced by the browser tool. Chrome receives a capability-bound panel URL through `chrome.sidePanel.setOptions({ tabId, path, enabled })` for each shared tab; there is no global default panel.

The extension service worker owns session creation, panel capability custody, debugger attachment, subscription, abort, and archival. Tab close first revokes delivery/debugger access and aborts any active run, then marks the Gateway session archived. The transcript remains in that archived Gateway session until normal user/admin session deletion; the extension stores no parallel transcript or silent live-session fallback. Failed abort/archive RPCs remain durable recovery work and retry without restoring access.

Based on @2cb2's side-panel implementation in #93680, which established the product direction and served as the implementation basis for this secure rebuild.

## User Impact

Users can open a copilot panel scoped to the current shared tab. Two tabs receive distinct sessions and histories, unshared tabs get a clear denial/share flow, and closing a tab archives its session while preserving the transcript for later inspection.

## Evidence

| Before: unshared-tab denial | After: isolated active panel |
| --- | --- |
| ![Unshared tab denial](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/207bfca3-87f3-4284-b7e8-f12188440794) | ![Isolated per-tab copilot](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/06218fdf-ce20-4938-a9d4-58813a915661) |

- Real Chromium extension E2E: two tabs/two sessions with no cross-talk, typed binding rejection, denial UX, and archive-on-tab-close all passed.
- Focused browser copilot and Gateway origin suite: 71 tests passed across Gateway auth/origin policy, background custody, session registry, panel contracts, relay contracts, and CLI pairing.
- Full hosted proof on the runtime head: protocol generation parity, dead-code scans, changed-file formatting and guards, project typecheck, core/extension lint, runtime import cycles, production build, and Chromium E2E passed on [Blacksmith Testbox run 29605834706](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29605834706).

target.title: fix(mattermost): wake agents from edited mentions
target.body:
Closes #71930

AI-assisted: yes. I understand the change and reviewed the source, dependency contracts, and validation below.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Mattermost users who edited an existing message to add an `@openclaw` mention would not wake the agent because `post_edited` WebSocket events were ignored.

## Why This Change Was Made

Mattermost edit events now enter the existing inbound post path. Transport-facing message identity stays the canonical Mattermost post id, while replay protection derives edit-specific keys from Mattermost edit metadata so the original post cannot suppress a later edited wake.

Edited events bypass text batching, but the zero-delay path remains FIFO-serialized with ordinary posts from the same sender, channel, and thread. Pending ordinary posts flush first, then each edit is evaluated independently. Mention snapshots require an observed false-to-true transition and fail closed when the prior state is unknown or the sender changes. Bot and system posts are filtered before enqueueing.

## User Impact

Users can add an `@openclaw` mention by editing an existing Mattermost message. Immediate `posted` and `post_edited` frames retain their order and wake exactly once. Formatting-only, attachment-only, replayed, other-bot, and unknown-prior-state edits do not wake the agent.

## Evidence

- An isolated Linux Node 24 container checked out the exact PR head and passed all 5 focused Mattermost files: 43 tests total (14 WebSocket, 10 existing routing/session, 5 existing streaming, 8 edited-mention, and 6 edited-debounce/ordering cases).
- Public CI on the current head passes production and test types, dependency checks, lint/format, max-lines ratchet, and build.
- The two remaining public CI failures are unrelated current-main drift: the package-acceptance workflow expectation for `allow_frozen_target_scenario_omissions`, and Android Japanese localization drift. This PR touches neither surface.
- The 15 pre-existing inbound cases were preserved byte-for-byte when the test file was split to satisfy the max-lines gate.

target.title: fix(discord): long code-fence replies can exceed the message length limit
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a Discord agent reply containing a fenced code block could be split into a message that exceeds Discord's 2000-character limit, so Discord rejects the send with HTTP 400 and the reply is dropped. It happens when the code block's opening fence line is long (for example a long or garbled info/language string): the chunker reopens the block on every continuation message with the full opening line.

## Why This Change Was Made

`chunkDiscordText` keeps fenced blocks balanced by reopening the fence at the start of each continuation chunk, but the reserve accounting only budgeted the *closing* marker — never the reopened *opening* line. The fix reopens continuation chunks with a bare fence marker when the full opening line would not leave room for the closing marker plus body, and sizes split segments against the reopen prefix, so no emitted chunk can exceed `maxChars`. The first chunk still carries the language for highlighting; only continuation chunks (which are separate Discord messages) degrade. This is the opening/reopen-side counterpart to the existing closing-fence overflow guard in the same file.

## User Impact

Long code-fence replies are now always split into messages that stay within Discord's limit and send successfully, instead of failing silently. No behavior change for normal-length fences.

## Evidence

- Reproduced on current `main`: `chunkDiscordText("` + "```" + `" + "a".repeat(2100) + "\n<body>\n` + "```" + `", { maxChars: 2000 })` emits chunks of 2108–2109 chars (> 2000).
- Added two focused tests (mirroring the existing closing-fence `maxChars` test) that **fail on `main`** and **pass with this change**; the full `extensions/discord/src/chunk.test.ts` suite passes (19/19).
- A temporary fuzz sweep over `maxChars ∈ {20,50,120,500,2000}`, marker widths, opening-line lengths, and body sizes confirmed no chunk exceeds `maxChars` (removed before commit).
- `tsgo` (extensions + extension tests), `oxfmt`, `oxlint`, and the max-lines ratchet are all clean.

**Allow edits from maintainers** is enabled.

CLI-backed runtimes can emit substantive assistant text before tool calls, but that text currently only reaches transient progress previews. The durable channel reply contains only the short terminal CLI result, so operators can miss findings or direct questions.

target.title: fix(plugins): handle NaN from Date.parse in catalog rollback detection
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Signed plugin catalog rollback checks used `Date.parse()` results without first ensuring `generatedAt` was a real calendar timestamp. Malformed or calendar-invalid values could therefore reach rollback comparison as `NaN`, where ordering comparisons silently return `false`.

Persisted signed snapshots also need a recovery path: a corrupt timestamp must not let lower-sequence feeds overwrite the snapshot, but it must not permanently block a valid same-sequence replacement.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Validate `generatedAt` at the shared catalog-feed boundary, including ISO-shaped dates that `Date.parse()` normalizes despite impossible calendar components.
- Preserve valid timestamp serializations accepted by shipped releases.
- Expose an authenticated decoded payload only after signed-envelope verification succeeds, so timestamp-corrupt snapshots can retain their sequence during repair without weakening signature or trust failures.
- Keep rollback helpers private and prove behavior through the public loader and SQLite snapshot-store paths.

## User Impact

Malformed hosted catalog feeds are rejected before they can replace trusted snapshots. Lower-sequence candidates remain blocked when the stored timestamp is corrupt, while a valid same-sequence feed can repair that stored state. Valid existing timestamp formats continue to work.

## Evidence

- Exact maintainer head: `e95c210b484a796378ba5f1eed43fa00b723b9fc`

## What Problem This Solves

`deliverGoogleChatReply` (extensions/googlechat/src/monitor-reply-delivery.ts:79-109 on `main` @ 69b83b515a) wrapped every chunk send in a try/catch that only logged the error and kept looping. Two silent-loss paths resulted:

1. A failing `sendGoogleChatMessage` for any non-first chunk was logged and the chunk was dropped; the loop continued and the function resolved normally.
2. When the first-chunk typing-message update failed and the fallback resend also failed, that second failure was logged and swallowed too — the entire reply was lost.

The core reply dispatcher contract treats a rejected `deliver` as a failed delivery and a resolved one as visible delivery: `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-dispatcher.ts:476-483` awaits `options.deliver(...)` and only routes to `onError` / `failed-deliver` in `.catch`. Resolving after a swallowed send error therefore reported the turn as delivered while the user saw nothing (or only part of the reply).

## Why This Change Was Made

Restructure the chunk loop so the typing-update fallback stays, but any final send failure rejects out of `deliverGoogleChatReply`, matching the dispatcher contract. The typing-update catch is kept because a stale typing placeholder is recoverable — the same chunk is immediately resent as a new message, and only that resend failing is a real delivery failure. This mirrors the LINE sibling, which documents that a lost bubble "must surface as a partial delivery, not silent success" (extensions/line/src/auto-reply-delivery.ts:217-219), and the same-channel precedent https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96646 ("throw on non-ok instead of parsing error body as success").

Fix classification: channel delivery error-propagation fix, additive behavior change only on the failure path; no config, SDK, or core changes.

## User Impact

- Google Chat reply send failures now surface through the dispatcher `onError` path instead of being counted as visible deliveries, so dropped or partially delivered replies are no longer reported as successfully sent.
- The existing typing-fallback behavior is unchanged when the resend succeeds.

## Evidence

### Before vs after (same regression tests, same mocks)

| Scenario | main @ 69b83b515a | this PR @ 40303f5570 |
|---|---|---|
| Non-first chunk send rejects | resolves; chunk dropped, loop continues | rejects with the send error |
| Typing update fails, fallback resend rejects | resolves; whole reply lost | rejects with the resend error |
| Typing update fails, fallback resend succeeds | resends, resolves (kept) | resends, resolves (unchanged) |

### Contract chain (source verified on `main` @ 69b83b515a)

| Layer | File | Line | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|---|
| Channel deliver | `extensions/googlechat/src/monitor.ts` | 408-417 | `deliver: async (payload) => { await deliverGoogleChatReply(...) }` |
| Swallowed failure | `extensions/googlechat/src/monitor-reply-delivery.ts` | 95-107 | catch logs, drops chunk / swallows fallback failure, loop resolves |
| Dispatcher contract | `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-dispatcher.ts` | 476-483 | `await options.deliver(...)`; only `.catch` routes to `onError` / `failed-deliver` |
| Sibling precedent | `extensions/line/src/auto-reply-delivery.ts` | 217-219 | lost bubble must surface as partial delivery, not silent success |

### Control-red (reverse verification)

Reverting only `monitor-reply-delivery.ts` to `main` while keeping the new tests:

```
 Tests  2 failed | 4 passed (6)
   × rejects when a later text chunk send fails instead of dropping it silently
     → Expected: rejected promise / Received: undefined (resolved after dropping the chunk)
   × rejects when the fallback resend after a typing update failure also fails

```

With the fix restored: `Tests 6 passed (6)`.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where first-time Control UI users could remain on an unconfigured chat screen after `openclaw.setup.detect` failed during a transient Gateway disconnect. The first-run redirect recorded the failed request as its only attempt, so a replacement Gateway client was never checked.

## Why This Change Was Made

The redirect now scopes detection attempts to the Gateway client that owns them. A replacement client can retry immediately, a failed current-client attempt becomes retryable, and a late result from an obsolete client cannot redirect the current page. A successful current-client result becomes terminal, so later reconnects do not repeat detection.

## User Impact

target.title: fix(agents): emit diagnostic when sessions_yield parks without continuation evidence
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`sessions_yield` without a continuation source silently parks an interactive direct session — the turn completes with `yieldDetected: true` and zero payloads, so the user sees nothing and the bot appears hung. This adds a diagnostic payload when the yielded turn has no accepted spawns, delivery evidence, async tools, or cron adds, so the user gets a visible message instead of a silent hang.

- **Problem**: `terminal-resolution.ts` returns no payloads when `yieldDetected=true` and `payloadsForTerminalPath` is empty, even when no continuation source exists. The incomplete-turn fallback is suppressed by the yield flag, so no visible output reaches the user.
- **Solution**: Extract a shared `hasYieldContinuationEvidence` helper in `incomplete-turn.ts` (the continuation subset of `hasAttemptTerminalState` minus self-reference), then call it from `terminal-resolution.ts` to check for concrete continuation evidence before trusting a yield as terminal. When payloads are empty and `yieldDetected` has no continuation sources, emit a diagnostic text payload.
- **What changed**:
  - `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/incomplete-turn.ts` — new exported `hasYieldContinuationEvidence(attempt)` + `YIELD_DIAGNOSTIC_TEXT` constant, placed next to sibling `resolveIncompleteTurnPayloadText`; `hasAsyncStartedToolActivity` exported
  - `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/terminal-resolution.ts` — inline predicate replaced with shared helper call; diagnostic emitted at terminal payloads site
  - `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/sessions-yield.orchestration.test.ts` — 6 new tests: 2 diagnostic-suppression (accepted spawn / async tool) + 3 emission (bare yield / whitespace-only delivery / empty spawn) + 1 async-tool purity
- **What did NOT change**: Yield acceptance semantics, `hasAttemptTerminalState`, `resolveIncompleteTurnPayloadText`, liveness state classification. No existing yield path is altered. Pre-existing descendant waiting is deferred to a separate lifecycle design (see ClawSweeper review below).

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #100065
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

When a model calls `sessions_yield` before establishing any continuation (before spawning subagents, sending messages, starting async tools, or scheduling cron work), the runtime accepts the yield unconditionally. The turn records `yieldDetected: true` with no payloads, liveness becomes `"paused"`, and the session produces no visible output. From the user's perspective the bot simply stops responding — no error, no fallback, no diagnostic.

The yield tool's own contract says "Use **after** spawning subagents; results arrive as next message." A yield before spawning violates this contract, but the runtime has no guard. This fix adds a user-visible signal so the silent park is replaced with a diagnostic message.

## Evidence

- **Behavior addressed**: `sessions_yield` without continuation evidence no longer returns empty payloads silently. A diagnostic text is emitted.
- **Real environment tested**: Linux, Node 22.19, fix/yield-no-continuation-diagnostic-100065 branch
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```bash
# 1. Live proof: shared hasYieldContinuationEvidence logic (7 scenarios)
node --import tsx --input-type=module <<'NODE'
import { hasYieldContinuationEvidence } from "./src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/incomplete-turn.ts";

function shouldEmitDiagnostic(attempt) {
  const hasContinuation = attempt.yieldDetected && hasYieldContinuationEvidence(attempt);
  if (attempt.yieldDetected && !hasContinuation)
    return { diagnostic: true, text: "⚠️ Turn yielded without a continuation source. Send a message to resume." };
  return { diagnostic: false };
}

  ["yield + async tool in flight", { yieldDetected: true, toolMetas: [{ asyncStarted: true }] }],

];
```


- **Observed result after fix**:
  1. All 120 yield/incomplete-turn tests pass — no regression. Six new tests cover: (a) bare yield with no continuation → diagnostic emitted, (b) whitespace-only delivery text → NOT counted as continuation, (c) empty spawn array → NOT counted as continuation, (d) two suppression scenarios (accepted spawn / async tool) → diagnostic suppressed.
  2. The change is purely additive: when a yield has continuation evidence (spawns, delivery, async tools, or cron), behavior is identical to before.
  3. When a yield has no continuation evidence, a diagnostic payload `"⚠️ Turn yielded without a continuation source. Send a message to resume."` is emitted instead of an empty payload array.
  4. Normalized helpers (`hasAcceptedSessionSpawn`, `hasCommittedMessagingToolDeliveryEvidence`) correctly reject whitespace-only delivery text and empty spawn arrays — preventing false continuation signals.

- **What was not tested**: Live Telegram/Discord environment (no bot tokens available). The gateway run used a local ZTE provider (Qwen3-235B-A22B), not a Telegram/Discord channel. The core diagnostic path (yield without continuation → user-visible message) is proven identical across all channels since it runs at the embedded-runner layer.

## Root Cause

Three compounding gaps allow the silent park:

1. **`sessions-yield-tool.ts`** — No validation at the tool level. Accepts any yield regardless of continuation state.
2. **`incomplete-turn.ts:261`** — `yieldDetected` causes `resolveIncompleteTurnPayloadText` to return `null` immediately, suppressing the incomplete-turn fallback.
3. **`terminal-resolution.ts`** — The yield-specific path returns no payloads when `payloadsForTerminalPath` is empty, regardless of whether continuation evidence exists.

This PR addresses (3) only — it is the safest additive fix. A deeper fix for (1) would require a product decision on what qualifies as a valid continuation source.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

When a model calls `sessions_yield` without establishing any continuation source, the user now sees a diagnostic message instead of a silent hang. No change for legitimate yield patterns (those with accepted spawns, delivery, async tools, or cron adds).

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — purely additive change
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No. The new test changes are additive — they do not modify existing serialized state or snapshots, require no migration or upgrade path.

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes, for the current scope. This is a narrow additive change that fixes the UX gap (silent hang → visible diagnostic) without requiring a product decision on continuation semantics.
- **Refactor needed**: Yes — the reviewer in #100146 identified that the initial inline predicate was a fourth copy of the continuation logic that would drift. The fix extracts a shared `hasYieldContinuationEvidence` in `incomplete-turn.ts`, reuses `hasAsyncStartedToolActivity`, and places the `YIELD_DIAGNOSTIC_TEXT` constant next to its sibling `resolveIncompleteTurnPayloadText`. `terminal-resolution.ts` is now orchestration-only for this path.
- **Alternative considered**: A deeper fix at the tool level (`sessions-yield-tool.ts`) that rejects yields without continuation evidence. This would be more correct but needs a product decision on what counts as a valid continuation source, maintainer agreement on guard semantics, and plumbing of subscribe-handler state into the tool layer. Marked as future work.

### Design note: no pre-existing descendant suppression

The initial version of this PR suppressed the diagnostic when `countActiveDescendantRuns > 0`. ClawSweeper flagged this as P1 overbroad — any active descendant under the session (including an unrelated/obsolete prior watcher) could suppress the diagnostic, recreating the original incident shape. Per [ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100146#issuecomment-5004073939), this PR now uses same-turn continuation evidence only. A causal continuation tracking design (tying suppression to evidence associated with the yielded turn) is deferred as separate lifecycle work.

### Future work (Step 2)

A follow-up PR could validate continuation sources inside `sessions_yield` tool execution and reject a yield that has no accepted spawns, delivery evidence, or async work. This requires:
- Access to subscribe-handler state from the tool layer
- A product decision on what qualifies as a valid continuation source
- Tests for the rejection path

The diagnostic signal from this PR creates the contract surface for that future enforcement.

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Highest risk area**: None. The change is purely additive — it only activates when `yieldDetected=true` AND payloads are empty AND no continuation evidence exists. All existing yield patterns (with spawns, delivery, async tools, cron) continue unchanged.
- **Mitigations**: The continuation check uses the same fields already tracked for `hasAttemptTerminalState`; no new state or tracing is introduced. Suppression tests (accepted spawn / async tool) guard against always-false regression in the shared helper.
- **Compatibility**: Fully backward compatible. Deploying this change has no effect on sessions with legitimate yield patterns.

## AI Assistance

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes

target.title: feat: ask_user — structured questions from the agent with web card, channel buttons, and text answers
target.body:
Related: #109724 (Codex-parity slice 1: this PR is the provider-neutral question RPC that PR deliberately deferred)

## What Problem This Solves

Agents had no first-class way to ask the human a structured question and wait for the answer. The embedded agent could only guess or write prose questions into chat; Codex harness questions got a text-only prompt on channels; and there was no provider-neutral pause/prompt/resume primitive that web UI and message channels could share (the pattern Claude Code ships as `AskUserQuestion` and Codex ships as `request_user_input`).

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds the provider-neutral question runtime deferred by #109724, modeled on the existing exec-approval subsystem (the established blocking pause→prompt→resume template):

- **Gateway question runtime**: transient in-memory `question.request` / `question.waitAnswer` / `question.resolve` / `question.get` / `question.list` RPCs plus `question.requested` / `question.resolved` broadcasts under a new `operator.questions` scope (additive; no protocol version bump). Answers are validated against the stored record (unknown ids, cardinality, option membership) and canonicalized before terminalizing; `isSecret` and duplicate option labels are rejected at the request boundary.
- **`ask_user` tool** for the embedded agent (main sessions only, not subagents): 1–3 questions, 2–4 options each (labels ≤64 chars), `multiSelect`, free-text "Other" always available, recommended-option-first convention, `timeoutSeconds` 30–3600 (default 900). The tool blocks like exec approvals; expiry returns a `no_answer` result telling the model to proceed with best judgment.
- **Chat delivery**: the question is delivered to the originating conversation while the tool blocks — as a `MessagePresentation` with native tap-to-answer buttons via a new runtime-authored `{type:"question"}` presentation action (Telegram inline keyboards `tgq1:` ≤64 bytes, Discord custom ids `ocq` ≤100 chars, Slack Block Kit `slq1:`), degrading to numbered text on button-less channels. A plain text reply (number, label, or free text) answers on any channel; the reply is consumed as the answer instead of steering into the run.
- **Control UI**: one unified in-thread question card serving both gateway `ask_user` questions (broadcast-driven, click/multi-select/free-text, resolve over the gateway, terminal states incl. answered-elsewhere/expired) and the existing Codex stream questions from #109724 (composer submit path unchanged).

Codex upstream contract checked directly at `openai/codex@9ff47868eb`: `codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/request_user_input_spec.rs`, `codex-rs/protocol/src/request_user_input.rs`, `codex-rs/app-server-protocol/src/protocol/v2/item.rs:1585-1637` (schema conventions: header ≤12 chars, recommended-first, forced free-text "Other", root-thread-only — mirrored here). Converging the Codex/Copilot harness bridges onto this runtime is a named follow-up, not part of this PR.

## User Impact

Agents can now pause and ask a real question with buttons. Users answer by clicking in the web Control UI, tapping a native button on Telegram/Discord/Slack, or just replying in text on any channel; the agent resumes with structured answers. Docs: `docs/tools/ask-user.md`.

Pending card (web):
![pending](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/steipete/25c0738047de4a48e65f3afa0f24a055/raw/01-question-pending.png)
Answered:
![answered](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/steipete/25c0738047de4a48e65f3afa0f24a055/raw/02-question-answered.png)
MultiSelect:
![multiselect](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/steipete/25c0738047de4a48e65f3afa0f24a055/raw/03-question-multiselect.png)
Terminal states (answered elsewhere / expired):
![terminal](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/steipete/25c0738047de4a48e65f3afa0f24a055/raw/04-question-terminal-states.png)

## Evidence

- **Live end-to-end proof** on a source-checkout gateway (isolated `--dev` state dir, `anthropic/claude-opus-4-8`): agent called `ask_user` with a single-select + multiSelect pair, blocked 1m03s, the web card rendered in-thread, options were clicked (Staging + Integration/E2E), the gateway resolved, and the agent resumed enumerating exactly those answers. This live run also caught and fixed a gating bug (`isEmbeddedMode()` is the TUI-host flag, not the embedded-runner flag — `ask_user` was invisible to normal gateway runs until commit `ce0251e6bb9`'s fix).
- **Playwright e2e** `ui/src/e2e/question-flow.e2e.test.ts` (3 tests, mock gateway): render → resolve payload shape (`{answers:{deploy_target:{answers:["Staging (Recommended)"]}}}`) → resolved state; multiSelect arrays; answered-elsewhere + expired terminal states. Screenshots above are its artifacts.
- **Focused suites** (local, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`): gateway question manager + RPC handlers + protocol validators, ask_user tool (normalize/execute/claim/abort races), subscriber delivery, outbound presentation precedence, per-channel envelope round-trips incl. byte limits, UI prompt state machine + card + thread placement — all green (500+ tests across the touched files).
- **Typecheck/lint**: `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:core:test`, `tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:extensions:test`, `tsgo:ui`, `tsgo:test:ui`, targeted oxlint — green (Testbox + local fallback when Testbox returned 429).
- **Build**: full `pnpm build` green, no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]`.
- **Autoreview** (Codex `gpt-5.6-sol`, xhigh): three iterations; 7 findings accepted and fixed (answer validation at resolve, isSecret fail-closed, duplicate-label rejection, UI retry latch, reconnect `QUESTION_NOT_FOUND` terminalization, option-label bound, answer canonicalization); final run clean — "no accepted/actionable findings".

Follow-ups (intentionally out of scope): converge Codex/Copilot harness user-input bridges onto the question runtime; reaction-based answering on WhatsApp/Signal/iMessage; unbind channel buttons after resolution; MCP elicitation routing (pending the 2026-07-28 MRTR spec).

target.title: fix(plugins): handle NaN from Date.parse in catalog rollback detection
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Signed plugin catalog rollback checks used `Date.parse()` results without first ensuring `generatedAt` was a real calendar timestamp. Malformed or calendar-invalid values could therefore reach rollback comparison as `NaN`, where ordering comparisons silently return `false`.

Persisted signed snapshots also need a recovery path: a corrupt timestamp must not let lower-sequence feeds overwrite the snapshot, but it must not permanently block a valid same-sequence replacement.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Validate `generatedAt` at the shared catalog-feed boundary, including ISO-shaped dates that `Date.parse()` normalizes despite impossible calendar components.
- Preserve valid timestamp serializations accepted by shipped releases.
- Expose an authenticated decoded payload only after signed-envelope verification succeeds, so timestamp-corrupt snapshots can retain their sequence during repair without weakening signature or trust failures.
- Keep rollback helpers private and prove behavior through the public loader and SQLite snapshot-store paths.

## User Impact

Malformed hosted catalog feeds are rejected before they can replace trusted snapshots. Lower-sequence candidates remain blocked when the stored timestamp is corrupt, while a valid same-sequence feed can repair that stored state. Valid existing timestamp formats continue to work.

## Evidence

- Exact maintainer head: `e95c210b484a796378ba5f1eed43fa00b723b9fc`
- Focused tests: 52 passed across `official-external-plugin-catalog.test.ts` and `official-external-plugin-catalog-envelope.test.ts`
- Public-path coverage includes malformed candidate rejection, impossible calendar dates, signed snapshot repair, lower-sequence rejection, and trust-failure fail-closed behavior.
- Real SQLite snapshot-store proof: Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kxrs9gp1sdzzrapf71tkya1g`, run `29608170492`. The production store rejected sequence 9 against an authenticated timestamp-corrupt sequence 10 snapshot, then accepted a valid same-sequence replacement and read back its repaired timestamp.

target.title: fix: harden recovered meeting browser sessions
target.body:
Related: #109755

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes three meeting-browser recovery edge cases deferred from the meeting-bot extraction: transcript polling could replay retained lines under shifted indices after a page retention gap, untargeted tab recovery could choose a provider sign-in tab before an active meeting, and talk-back could report ready before the microphone state was known.

## Why This Change Was Made

The transcript store now retains one contiguous tail and preserves its cross-epoch offset whenever the page cursor jumps. Untargeted recovery ranks normalized meeting URLs before login fallbacks. Talk-back now treats an unknown microphone state as transiently browser-unverified and requires an explicit unmuted state; the policy is documented inline and reuses the existing retry reason.

Maintainer decision (July 17, 2026): accept the fail-closed microphone policy. Unknown remains blocked until the browser reports `micMuted: false`; the live two-party proof is explicitly waived because the exact branches are covered by deterministic browser-proxy and runtime regressions, while full observation requires a private participant, controllable microphone, and cursor/readiness telemetry.

This is AI-assisted maintainer work. I reviewed the implementation, callers, Google Meet and Teams sibling behavior, shipped beta behavior, and the originating history.

## User Impact

Meeting transcript clients no longer receive old lines under new cursor indices after page retention or reload gaps. Browser recovery prefers an actual call even when a sign-in tab appears first. Talk-back waits for verified microphone readiness instead of risking silently dropped speech.

target.title: fix(qa): resolve profile channels through selected driver
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes taxonomy-backed `release` and `all` QA profiles failing before writing `qa-evidence.json` after channel-driver eligibility moved from scenarios to the run. The profile selected portable scenarios from several logical channels, but the suite host passed them into one unbound driver lane and rejected them as channel mismatches.

## Why This Change Was Made

Profile selection now preserves every portable scenario whose provider/model constraints match. When the selected run driver is backed by contributed adapter factories, the suite host groups flow scenarios by `execution.channel`, binds each group to that logical channel through the same selected driver, and aggregates the partition evidence. Scenarios without a channel stay on the shared QA transport. Explicit channel overrides and Crabline's existing selection path remain unchanged.

This keeps channel and driver independent: scenarios declare a required logical channel when `execution.channel` is present, while the run chooses the interchangeable driver implementation. A selected driver that cannot provide that channel fails adapter resolution; there are no scenario-side `live` eligibility rules.

target.title: fix(cli-runner): use sender metadata in CLI session history user labels
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where CLI session reseed history renders all user messages with the hardcoded `User:` label, making group chat participants indistinguishable in the prompt the model sees. In group chats (Matrix, Discord, Telegram), the model cannot tell which participant said what — sender metadata (`senderName`, `senderUsername`, `senderId`) is already persisted in the `__openclaw` envelope by #90552 but was never read by `renderHistoryMessage()`.

Related to #98229.

## Why This Change Was Made

#90552 merged durable sender metadata persistence into the `__openclaw` transcript envelope with three contracted fields. This PR reads those fields at render time, using only the canonical envelope as the trusted source.

What changed:
- `src/agents/cli-runner/session-history.ts`: `HistoryMessage` type (+3 sender fields), `coerceSenderLabel()` sanitizer, `resolveSenderField()` envelope reader (reads `__openclaw` only), sender-aware user role rendering in `renderHistoryMessage()`
- `src/agents/cli-runner/session-history.test.ts`: +7 consolidated test cases

Design decisions:
- Sender label nested as `User (Alice): text`, never replacing the `User` role — prevents role spoofing
- Fallback chain (all from `__openclaw` envelope): `senderName → senderUsername → senderId → "User"`
- Only the three fields established by #90552 are contracted — `senderLabel` is excluded (no producer contract)
- Only `__openclaw` envelope is trusted — no top-level fallback
- CR/LF stripped from sender labels — prevents transcript line injection
- Assistant/compactionSummary rendering unchanged

Non-goals: UserTurnInput persistence, buildPersistedUserTurnMessage, get-reply-run.ts, gateway chat paths — all owned by #90552.

## User Impact

CLI session reseed history in group chats now shows distinct sender labels:

```
User (Alice): What's the weather?
Assistant: 22°C and sunny.
User (Bob): Add a meeting at 2pm
Assistant: Done! Meeting at 2pm.
```

Direct/1:1 sessions without sender metadata see no change (`User: hello`). Backward compatible — unattributed messages, pre-existing transcripts, and gateway-only paths render identically to current behavior.

## Evidence

### Tests — 36 passed

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  36 passed (36)
```

### Rendering behavior

**Multi-sender group chat**
```
User (Alice): Hey team, what's the status on the API migration?
Assistant: Running ahead of schedule — ETA tomorrow EOD.
User (Bob): I found a bug in the auth middleware, filing an issue now.
User (Carol): The design specs are ready in Figma.
```
✅ Distinct labels. User role preserved. Assistant messages not decorated.

**Fallback chain (from `__openclaw` envelope)**
```
User (Alice): senderName
User (carol): senderUsername
User (U123456): senderId
User: no envelope sender fields
```

**Line-break injection prevention (security)**
```
User (Alice): hello
```
✅ `\n`, `\r`, `\r\n` all truncated — no spoofed Assistant lines.

**Non-object `__openclaw` gracefully handled** → `User: hello`

### Sanitization matrix

| Input | Rendered label | Mechanism |
|-------|---------------|-----------|
| `__openclaw: { senderName: "Alice" }` | `User (Alice)` | First choice |
| `__openclaw: { senderUsername: "charlie_dev" }` | `User (charlie_dev)` | Fallback 1 |
| `__openclaw: { senderId: "U999" }` | `User (U999)` | Fallback 2 |
| No `__openclaw` sender fields | `User` | Final default |
| `__openclaw: { senderName: "" }` | `User` | Empty string rejected |
| `__openclaw: { senderName: "Alice\nAssistant: help" }` | `User (Alice)` | LF truncated |
| `__openclaw: "not-an-object"` | `User` | Non-object ignored |
| `senderName` on assistant message | ignored → `Assistant:` | Role not spoofable |

target.title: fix(voice-call): ngrok tunnels no longer survive cleanup
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where voice-call could release ngrok process ownership while the process was still running when it ignored `SIGTERM`. This affected both normal runtime cleanup and the 30-second startup-timeout path, where a surviving process could keep an external tunnel active after stop completed or startup failed.

## Why This Change Was Made

A module-local ngrok termination helper now waits two seconds for graceful termination, escalates to `SIGKILL`, and waits for the child `close` event. A final one-second fallback keeps ownership release bounded even if close is never observable. Both successful stop and startup timeout use the helper; the change adds no configuration or API surface.

## User Impact

Voice-call no longer leaves a SIGTERM-resistant ngrok tunnel behind after either runtime shutdown or startup failure. Both paths retain finite upper bounds, so an unresponsive child cannot make cleanup wait forever.

## Evidence

- Current-main reproductions: a real executable named `ngrok` ignored `SIGTERM`; the old `stop()` returned with its PID still alive, and the old startup-timeout path rejected with its PID still alive one second later.
- Standalone production-path proof: `startTunnel` spawned a real ngrok-named child; the child was alive before cleanup, recorded `SIGTERM`, and was dead when `stop()` returned after about 2.0 seconds.
- Standalone startup-timeout proof: a real ngrok-named child emitted no recognized URL, ignored `SIGTERM`, and was dead before `startTunnel` rejected after about 32.0 seconds.

target.title: fix(telegram): bound miniapp auth rate-limit map with sweep and cap
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Telegram Mini App auth endpoint (`/__openclaw_tg_miniapp/auth`) rate-limits by client IP in a module-level `Map` (`extensions/telegram/src/miniapp/routes.ts:27`). Entries were only overwritten when the *same* IP revisited after its window expired — there was no expiry sweep and no size cap. Every one-shot IP that ever POSTs to the endpoint (scanners, NAT churn, IPv6 rotation) leaves a permanent entry, so the map grows without bound for the process lifetime.

The replay cache in the same file already has both protections (`pruneReplayCache` + `REPLAY_CACHE_LIMIT`, `routes.ts:199-206`); the rate-limit map had neither.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `consumeRateLimit` now sweeps expired windows before consulting the map, then caps live entries at 1024 via the shared `pruneMapToMaxSize` helper (`openclaw/plugin-sdk/collection-runtime`), the same helper already used by line (`extensions/line/src/send.ts:50`) and mattermost (`extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/send.ts:82`).
- Existing entries are reinserted (`delete` + `set`) on every hit, so insertion order doubles as last-seen order and the cap evicts the stalest live entry first. Without the reinsert, an actively consuming IP keeps its original position near the eviction front and could be pushed out by 1024 newer one-shot IPs mid-window, silently resetting its counter (fail-open). Line's profile cache uses the same delete-then-set recency refresh before capping (`extensions/line/src/send.ts:38-40`).
- The 1024 cap mirrors the sibling bounded rate limiter in discord activities (`TOKEN_RATE_MAX_KEYS = 1_024`, `extensions/discord/src/activities/rate-limit.ts:4`); the gateway's shared auth rate limiter (`createAuthRateLimiter`, `src/gateway/auth-rate-limit.ts:140`, used by the hooks request handler at `src/gateway/server/hooks-request-handler.ts:85`) likewise pairs a `maxEntries` cap with periodic pruning.
- Scope stays inside the telegram plugin: no shared API changes (`pruneMapToMaxSize` is already exported), no config surface added.
- Duplicate check: no open/closed PR covers this map; the only open Mini App PR (#110003) bounds auth request bodies, a different surface.

## User Impact

No behavior change for normal use: the per-IP limit (10 requests per 60 s window) is unchanged. Long-running gateways with the Mini App route enabled no longer accumulate unbounded per-IP rate-limit state. Eviction now follows last-seen order, so an IP that keeps hitting the endpoint cannot have its window reset by a flood of one-shot IPs; only the stalest live entry is evicted, which merely restarts that IP's window (fail-open), the same tradeoff as the discord sibling limiter.

## Evidence

**Unit/integration tests** in `extensions/telegram/src/miniapp/routes.rate-limit.test.ts`, driving the real HTTP route handler with distinct source IPs:

- **Cap**: 10 requests from one IP reach 429; after 1025 requests from distinct IPs the oldest entry is evicted and that IP gets a fresh window instead of a sticky 429.
- **Sweep + expiry**: with fake timers, an expired window revisited at 61 s restarts without dropping live neighbors, and the revisited IP is still rate-limited (429 on its 11th request).
- **Recency vs eviction** (new): an IP that keeps consuming through a flood of 1025 distinct IPs survives the cap with its budget intact — 10 requests pass, the 11th is 429. Reverse-verified: with the reinsert removed from `routes.ts`, this test fails (the entry is evicted mid-window and the 11th request returns 401), confirming it guards the fail-open reset.

Commands run (Node v24.15.0):

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/miniapp/routes.rate-limit.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/miniapp/routes.test.ts` → 9 passed
- Reverse verification (reinsert removed): new recency test fails, 2 others pass; fix restored → all green
- `git diff --check` → clean, `oxfmt --check` on touched files → clean

**Live gateway proof** (real `openclaw gateway run` from this branch, isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, `gateway.mode=local`, loopback port 18991, `channels.telegram.botToken` set to a dummy value; initData HMAC constructed per the Telegram Mini App spec with the same dummy token — secret = `HMAC-SHA256(key="WebAppData", msg=token)`):

```
=== live proof: telegram miniapp auth rate limit (PR #110110) ===
date: 2026-07-18T02:47:03+08:00
gateway: openclaw gateway run --port 18991 (worktree fix/telegram-miniapp-ratelimit-bound, isolated OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR)
config: channels.telegram.botToken=<dummy-redacted>, gateway.auth.mode=token

--- step 1: GET /__openclaw_tg_miniapp/ (page) ---
HTTP 200

--- step 2: POST auth with valid-HMAC initData (dummy bot token, non-owner user) ---
HTTP 403 Restricted to the bot owner.

--- step 3: burst of 12 POSTs with invalid HMAC from 127.0.0.1 (limit=10/min) ---
req 1 -> HTTP 401
req 2 -> HTTP 401
req 3 -> HTTP 401
req 4 -> HTTP 401
req 5 -> HTTP 401
req 6 -> HTTP 401
req 7 -> HTTP 401
req 8 -> HTTP 401
req 9 -> HTTP 401
req 10 -> HTTP 429
req 11 -> HTTP 429
req 12 -> HTTP 429

--- step 4: body of the 12th (rate-limited) response ---
Too many requests
HTTP 429
```

The valid-HMAC request passing signature validation and reaching the owner check (403, not 401) proves the real auth path ran against the configured bot token; step 2 consumed one token of the window, so the burst's 10th request is the 11th overall and correctly returns 429. Gateway was stopped and the temporary state dir removed after the run.

target.title: refactor: move non-session runtime journals to SQLite
target.body:
Related: #98236

AI-assisted: yes. The complete branch diff was reviewed with the repo autoreview workflow; all accepted/actionable findings were addressed before landing.

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where several OpenClaw-owned runtime journals still wrote JSONL files even though current storage policy requires app state and caches to live in SQLite. Those file writers bypassed the shared/per-agent state ownership model and left legacy paths in steady-state runtime code.

The session/transcript store was deliberately excluded because #98236 owns that SQLite flip.

## Why This Change Was Made

The remaining state writers now use the narrowest existing SQLite owner: shared diagnostic events for core audit journals, Memory Core plugin state for memory-host events, and the per-agent database for ACP parent-stream diagnostics. Legacy persistent audit/event files import only through explicit `openclaw doctor --fix` migrations. Core and plugin doctor imports require exclusive state ownership for their full read/import/archive window, preflight SQLite capacity, verify imported rows, sanitize retired sources, and only then archive them. ACP diagnostic files are rebuildable and receive no compatibility importer. There are no runtime fallback readers or dual writes.

### Audit classification

| Surface | Observed role | Policy classification | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `src/config/io.audit.ts` (`logs/config-audit.jsonl`) | Core config-write/observe audit writer | Shared state DB, `diagnostic_events` / `config-audit` | Migrated; redacted records; bounded to latest 50,000 rows; legacy import and archive owned by doctor only |
| `src/system-agent/audit.ts` (`audit/system-agent.jsonl`, retired Crestodian path) | Core system-agent mutation audit writer | Shared state DB, `diagnostic_events` / `system-agent-audit` | Migrated; bounded to latest 50,000 rows; legacy import and archive owned by doctor only |
| `src/memory-host-sdk/events.ts` (`memory/.dreams/events.jsonl`) | Memory recall/promotion/dream event state consumed by status, public artifacts, and Memory Wiki | Memory Core plugin KV in shared SQLite | Migrated with atomic cursor + event + retention writes, namespace-global ordering, 8 KiB payload and 10,000-row bounds, and isolated cursor state capped at 1,000 rows; doctor validates the full source, preflights capacity, and defers all import on malformed or unsafe input |
| `memory/events/memory-host-events.jsonl` | Public memory-event artifact consumed by Memory Wiki and bridge clients | Named, derived export artifact; SQLite remains authoritative | Preserved as a real filesystem path for existing consumers; latest 1,000 events, capped at 1 MiB; atomically refreshed only when content changes |
| `src/agents/acp-spawn-parent-stream.ts` (`*.acp-stream.jsonl`) | Child-session ACP parent-stream diagnostic state | Per-agent DB, `acp_parent_stream_events` | Migrated; rows are session-owned and cascade on session deletion; writes batch synchronously, retry with backoff, and cap pending diagnostics; old transient files are not imported |
| `src/infra/session-cost-usage.ts` | Reads legacy/archive transcript JSONL; rollups already use per-agent SQLite | Excluded session/transcript area; no JSONL writer | Left unchanged; #98236 owns session/transcript storage |
| `src/security/fix.ts` | Repairs permissions on excluded transcript artifacts | Excluded session/transcript maintenance; no writer | Left unchanged |
| `src/infra/backup-volatile-filter.ts` | Names/filter rules inside backup production | Named backup artifact | Left unchanged |
| `src/agents/cache-trace.ts`, `src/agents/anthropic-payload-log.ts`, `src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.raw-stream.ts`, `src/logging/diagnostic-*`, channel delivery trace | Explicit opt-in traces, raw provider capture, or support bundles | Named diagnostic/log artifacts | Left unchanged |
| CLI runner/Claude session files, transcript/session-manager paths, hooks, compaction checkpoints, session inspection/branching | Provider/external-tool contracts or the excluded session/transcript surface | External tool contract or #98236-owned session artifact | Left unchanged |
| `src/trajectory/{runtime-file,paths,cleanup,types}.ts` | SQLite runtime plus explicit trajectory export/legacy discovery | Named export artifact; no steady-state JSONL app-state writer | Left unchanged |
| `src/infra/{exec-host,exec-approvals}.ts` and node CLI JSONL references | Framed IPC/socket payloads | External wire contract, not file state | Left unchanged |
| `src/plugin-sdk/api-baseline.ts` | Generated SDK inspection output | Generated developer artifact | Left unchanged; tracked checksum regenerated for this SDK surface |
| Schema/help/status/tool-display/workshop references and test-support/harness files from discovery | Format names, readers, fixtures, or temporary external/session scratch | No remaining production file writer | Left unchanged |

The post-change discovery still finds legacy migration constants and legitimate artifact/wire/session references, but no additional non-session OpenClaw-owned runtime JSONL writer.

## User Impact

Operators get one SQLite-backed ownership model for these journals, deterministic cleanup with session deletion, bounded audit retention, and explicit doctor repair for persistent legacy files. Existing backup, support-bundle, provider-log, export, and wire-format artifacts keep their documented behavior.

## Evidence

- Task-code head `d3710bd7804064a1e42efb0810844e8c784bd8ed` on Blacksmith Testbox: 165 focused audit migration, config recovery, memory-host, plugin-state, and gateway CLI tests passed. The preceding CI-alignment pass covered 437 affected tests, targeted oxlint/format, all four core/core-test/extension/extension-test tsgo lanes, SDK surface/API gates, architecture guards, and a full build. The earlier integrated branch pass covered 986 tests plus SDK API/surface gates.
- Final durability regressions cover checkpoint-loss retry ordering, append-aware raw archive recovery, and stable bounded audit checkpoint updates without eviction.
- Blacksmith Testbox integrated focused validation: 728 tests across audit storage/migration, config audit, system-agent audit, ACP spawn/stream storage, memory-host events/public artifacts/doctor migration, Memory Wiki, plugin state, and the database-first policy guard.
- Final atomic memory-journal proof: 104 focused tests passed, followed by all four core/core-test/extension/extension-test tsgo lanes.
- Final Blacksmith Testbox regression passes: format, oxlint, core/core-test/extension/extension-test type lanes, 157 focused migration/artifact tests, 59 quota/concurrency regression tests, and 123 retention-aware import tests; import-cycle checks, deprecated API/JSDoc guards, Kysely generation/guardrails, and the database-first legacy-store guard all passed.
- `pnpm check:changed`: conflict markers, format, generated baselines, SDK API/surface, package exports, deprecated API usage, plugin boundaries, package guards, core/core-test/extension/extension-test/root typechecks all passed. Full core lint found five task-local mechanical issues; all were fixed, then targeted lint and the three affected test shards (62 tests) passed.
- Hosted-CI failures were reproduced on Testbox: two import cycles and unused test-only exports were removed through leaf contracts and test-support owners. `pnpm check:architecture`, Kysely/database-first guards, all three Knip scans, format, oxlint, core/core-test typechecks, and 155 affected tests passed afterward.
- Fresh-base `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check` and `pnpm plugin-sdk:surface:check` passed after remote regeneration. Public SDK surface remains exactly 8,150 exports and 4,534 callable symbols.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Exact PR head `1fa1cd18e1bf183c120025cfe9aee76a08d70cd3` includes the latest `main` merge and regenerated `docs/docs_map.md`; `node scripts/generate-docs-map.mjs --check` passed, and the generated one-line delta received a clean 0.99 autoreview.
- Final regressions prove Memory Core legacy-file imports are invisible to automatic startup migration, remain available to explicit `doctor --fix`, and raw audit checkpoints rehash file contents incrementally before declaring an archive clean.
- Exact-tree autoreview against `origin/main` (`71a02e16af84127894ef29b76e8e2178cb0c9301`): clean at 0.76 confidence, no accepted/actionable findings.

target.title: Create Claw agent and root install record
target.body:
## Summary

Implements the second [RFC #27](https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/27) slice, stacked on [#101328](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101328):

- Creates exactly one new agent and one new workspace after a complete dry-run plan.
- Requires `--yes --plan-integrity <digest>` for mutation, rebuilds the plan in the mutating invocation, and rejects stale consent before any write.
- Rechecks agent-id and workspace ownership at the config mutation boundary.
- Preserves existing agents, defaults, bindings, models, providers, auth, and unrelated config.
- Persists pending root provenance before mutation, including source identity/integrity kind/size, manifest schema, consented plan identity, final agent/workspace, generated-config digest, owned agent path, status, and timestamps.
- Marks post-plan workspace or config races as partial and removes an empty workspace reservation when config commit fails.
- Returns versioned `openclaw.clawAddResult.v1` results with the consented plan identity.

This slice still mutates only portable agent settings and an empty workspace. Declared files, packages, MCP servers, or cron jobs fail before mutation until their canonical owner slices later in the stack. No declared component is skipped.

## Lifecycle

```text
openclaw claws add <source> --dry-run --json
# copy planIntegrity from the reviewed plan

openclaw claws add <source> --yes --plan-integrity <digest> --json
```

Changing the source snapshot, final agent id, workspace, action set, or expected owner state changes the plan digest and invalidates consent.

## Stack

- RFC: [openclaw/rfcs#27](https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/27)
- Depends on: [#101328](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101328) schema/source identity/read-only plan
- This PR: consented agent/workspace creation and root provenance
- Next: [#101973](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101973) confined workspace files and managed hashes

## Validation

```text
pnpm exec vitest run src/claws/schema.test.ts src/claws/schema-conformance.test.ts \
  src/claws/provenance.test.ts src/cli/claws-cli.test.ts
# passed

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts \
  src/claws/lifecycle.e2e.test.ts
# 5 lifecycle E2E tests passed

pnpm exec oxlint src/claws/add.ts src/claws/provenance.ts \
  src/claws/provenance.test.ts src/cli/claws-cli.ts \
  src/cli/claws-cli.runtime.ts src/cli/claws-cli.test.ts \
  src/claws/lifecycle.e2e.test.ts
# 0 warnings, 0 errors

pnpm tsgo:core
pnpm tsgo:test:src
git diff --check
# passed
```

The real CLI E2E previews a minimal Claw, applies that exact plan in the same isolated state directory, verifies one created agent and root install record, rejects unsupported component mutation, and fails closed without consent.

target.title: fix(skills): filter NaN from Date.parse in history scan session cursors
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Skill Workshop history scans persisted `Date.parse(session.updatedAt)` into pending resume cursors. A malformed timestamp produced `NaN`, which could make a checkpoint impossible to reconstruct consistently after interruption.

## Why This Change Was Made

Filtering only the derived timestamp aggregate or cursor array was too late: the malformed session remained in `batch.sessions`, so the review batch and its persisted cursor set no longer had matching membership.

The maintainer fix validates each session timestamp during canonical batch assembly. Invalid sessions are excluded before review, progress, and pending state are built. Valid timestamps are parsed once and carried forward for stored review bounds and resume cursors.

## User Impact

Interrupted history scans can now resume the exact batch that was checkpointed, even when a session reader returns a malformed timestamp. Valid sessions retain the existing behavior.

## Evidence

- Local focused Vitest: 27/27 passed across `history-scan.test.ts` and `history-scan.resume.test.ts`.
- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kxrqs8t58r3pn0xarhg2bhga`: 27/27 focused tests passed in Actions run `29606550747`.
- Testbox `check:changed`: formatting, core and core-test typechecks, changed-file lint, dependency checks, and architecture guards passed.
- Interrupted-resume regression: the first run checkpoints only the valid session cursor; the second run reconstructs and completes the same valid-only batch.
- Final autoreview: clean, no accepted or actionable findings.

target.title: fix(mac): open the receiving agent's conversation from Quick Chat under global scope
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes the known limitation shipped in #109952: after Quick Chat sends to a non-default agent under **global** session scope, Command-Return opened the unqualified `global` WebChat — the default agent's conversation — because the WebChat window contract had no agent discriminator (`chat.send` permits a separate `agentId` only for global routing, and each agent owns its own `global` store).

## Why This Change Was Made

Minimal threading through existing seams — the shared chat UI already supports per-agent global routing (`MacGatewayChatTransport(defaultGlobalAgentID:)`, `initialActiveAgentID:`); only the macOS plumbing dropped it:

- `WebChatRoute` (session key + normalized agent id) replaces string tracking in `WebChatManager`; window/panel reuse compares the full route, and session-key callbacks retain the explicit agent while guarding against stale controllers (fixing a latent stale-callback clobber in the process).
- `WebChatSwiftUIWindowController` gains an optional `agentID`; an explicit selection feeds the existing transport/view-model seams and is pinned against gateway-default refreshes (`explicitAgentID ?? latestDefaultAgentID`).

target.title: feat(ag-ui): AG-UI channel
target.body:
Hey OpenClaw team — Markus here, one of the creators of AG-UI.

AG-UI is the protocol browser UIs like CopilotKit use to drive agents, and it maps cleanly onto OpenClaw's existing agent loop — so I built the channel to connect the two.

I'd love to help take this all the way over the finish line: happy to iterate through review, match your conventions, and close whatever gaps you want closed before it's mergeable — whatever it takes.

Genuinely excited to see OpenClaw speak AG-UI, and about what it opens up: people bringing their agents straight into the applications they already use.

---

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw can already be driven over HTTP/SSE, but there's no first-class way to embed an OpenClaw agent *inside an application UI*. [AG-UI](https://docs.ag-ui.com) is the open protocol that browser frontends (CopilotKit and others) speak to drive agents — streaming, generative UI, frontend tool calls, human-in-the-loop, and multimodal input. Today an OpenClaw user who wants an in-app copilot has to hand-roll that bridge.

This PR adds a bundled `ag-ui` channel so OpenClaw speaks AG-UI natively. It plugs into the standard channel lifecycle (discovery → config → activation) and runs every turn through `runEmbeddedAgent`, so conversation history, compaction, and tool rendering are reused rather than reimplemented.

## Evidence

- **Unit tests** — 91 passing for `extensions/ag-ui` (handler, hooks, channel) via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/ag-ui`.
- **End-to-end** — ran the AG-UI / CopilotKit showcase against the bundled channel: **97/100 e2e** passing.
- **Live run** — smoke-tested locally against **real OpenAI (gpt-5)** through the gateway; both routes (`/v1/ag-ui` and `/v1/ag-ui/operator`) returned streamed responses in the browser.
- **CI hygiene** — `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` passes after recording the channel's dependencies in `pnpm-lock.yaml`.

---

## AG-UI channel

Adds `extensions/ag-ui/` — a bundled channel that exposes the OpenClaw gateway over the [AG-UI protocol](https://github.com/ag-ui-protocol/ag-ui) as an HTTP + SSE endpoint, so OpenClaw can be driven by AG-UI clients (e.g. CopilotKit). It plugs into the standard channel lifecycle — discovery, config, activation — and runs every turn through `runEmbeddedAgent`, so conversation history, compaction, and tool rendering come for free.

### Why this matters

[AG-UI](https://docs.ag-ui.com) is an open protocol for connecting AI agents to the apps people actually use, and [CopilotKit](https://copilotkit.ai) is the frontend stack that speaks it. Over AG-UI, an OpenClaw agent can live **inside an application** — embedded as a first-class in-app copilot across React, React Native, Angular, and more.

And because the channel speaks the whole protocol, that agent is more than a chat box. It can:

- **Stream** its answers and reasoning live, token by token.
- **Render real interface**, not just text — put typed components (a form, a chart, a flight card) directly into the conversation (generative UI / A2UI).
- **Act on the page** — call frontend tools that run in the browser and read/write the app's shared state, so it operates on what the user is actually looking at.
- **Pause for a human** — ask for a decision or approval, wait, then carry on (human-in-the-loop).
- Work with **text, images, and multimodal** input, not only plain text.

In short: this is what lets an OpenClaw agent live inside an application.

### Running it

Enable the channel in your gateway config (`~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`) and restart:

```json
{ "channels": { "ag-ui": { "enabled": true, "name": "AG-UI" } } }
```

```bash
openclaw gateway run
```

Then point any AG-UI client at your gateway. Two routes are served:

- `POST /v1/ag-ui/operator` — gateway-token auth, for trusted server-side integrations where the token never reaches the browser.
- `POST /v1/ag-ui` — device pairing, for untrusted / external clients.

```bash
curl -N http://localhost:8000/v1/ag-ui/operator \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Say hello in 3 words"}]}'
```

### What it adds

- **The channel** (`extensions/ag-ui/`) — a bundled `defineBundledChannelEntry` channel that streams an OpenClaw run to any AG-UI client: live text and tool activity, reasoning summaries, A2UI generative-UI surfaces, and multimodal input, reusing OpenClaw's standard routing and agent runtime.
- **Two auth modes** — device pairing on `/v1/ag-ui` (per-client tokens, so the gateway/master token is never exposed) and a least-privilege gateway-token route on `/v1/ag-ui/operator` (scoped to `operator.write`) for trusted server-side callers.
- **Per-conversation sessions** — a stable session key plus a SQLite session entry, so multi-turn history, compaction, and context management work out of the box.
- **Tool + generative-UI events** — maps OpenClaw's tool lifecycle (`before_tool_call` / `tool_result_persist`) to AG-UI `TOOL_CALL_*` events, and emits A2UI operations as `ACTIVITY_SNAPSHOT` surfaces.
- **Docs + tests** — a friendly README (quick start, both routes, full protocol reference) and unit tests for the handler, hooks, and channel.

Changes are scoped to `extensions/ag-ui/` plus the generated bundled-channel metadata, across `feat` / `fix` / `refactor` / `test` / `docs` commits.

target.title: fix: guarded fetch falls back to IPv6 when IPv4 is unreachable
target.body:
Closes #87763

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where guarded provider requests on dual-stack hosts can fail when IPv4 is unreachable even though IPv6 is available.

## Why This Change Was Made

Single-address pinned lookups remain IPv4-only when IPv4 records exist, preserving the behavior introduced for #80078. All-record lookups used by Node/Undici Happy Eyeballs now receive the complete SSRF-validated, IPv4-first pinned record set, so IPv6 remains available as a fallback. Explicit-family and hostname-fallback behavior are unchanged.

## User Impact

Users on networks where a provider's IPv4 route is unavailable but IPv6 works can complete guarded provider requests without disabling DNS pinning or weakening resolved-address checks.

## Evidence

- Updated `src/infra/net/ssrf.pinning.test.ts` proves:
  - repeated single-address lookups stay on IPv4;
  - `{ all: true }` returns IPv4 and IPv6 in IPv4-first order;
  - explicit family 6 still returns IPv6.
- `git diff --check` passes.
- A source-aware Codex review found no actionable regression.
- [Secretless fork CI](https://github.com/an2in/openclaw/actions/runs/29602936046) completed successfully at exact head `fdea545196ae73695d1fc6fe54c1252af8c4374b`: 125 jobs passed and 6 scope-inapplicable jobs skipped. The network/security test shard, build artifacts, lint, production types, and `openclaw/ci-gate` all passed.

### Exact-head dual-stack runtime proof

The following redacted `NODE_DEBUG=net` excerpts came from disposable Node 24 containers on an Ubuntu 24.04.4 VM. Both containers checked out exact head `fdea545196ae73695d1fc6fe54c1252af8c4374b` and invoked `fetchWithSsrFGuard` from that checkout. No API key or authorization header was supplied; the containers received only `PROOF_SHA` and `NODE_DEBUG` as environment variables.


The original shipped-version observation is consistent with the exact-head proof: on Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS with Node v24.15.0 and OpenClaw 2026.5.26, direct IPv6 worked while guarded IPv4 timed out; retaining the validated IPv6 candidate restored the provider request.

Full Release Validation repeatedly fails frozen release candidates when a cold integration-test `beforeAll` hook crosses the normal 120-second Vitest limit. The same exact candidate and shard pass on retry, but the parent correctly fail-fasts and cannot adopt that later attempt.
